author: WP20
summary: An alpha.1-era case study of free-direct's call-site audits of the free-eggbert (Speedy Eggbert 2) reconstruction and Planet Blupi, plus a native-CNA feasibility study for Free Eggbert. The sibling facts were re-read at free-direct 934f72f and free-eggbert 7ea63d1 and the CNA facts (CNJ colour key, Song extensions, SDL_mixer MIDI options, default timestep) at TARGET; naming and a few details were corrected. The site had only one-line mentions of free-direct and nothing on these audits; they now live on a new porting case-studies page next to the Speedy Blupi 2013 port.

concepts.section: Case Study: Speedy Blupi and Planet Blupi
concepts.text: Two legacy Windows games shaped free-direct's scope: the free-eggbert reconstruction of Speedy Eggbert 2 and Epsitec's published Planet Blupi source; both run through the compatibility layer, while a native-CNA port of Free Eggbert is only a proposal.
concepts.note: Corrected naming: free-eggbert reconstructs Speedy Eggbert 2 (not the 2013 Speedy Blupi, which is mobile-eggbert); pins added; neither decompiled game is called open source.

target.evidence: free-eggbert @7ea63d1 README (Speedy Eggbert 2 reconstruction); planetblupi @8e42e1c README

concepts.text: free-direct's subsystem boundaries come from call-site audits of the two games; both use DirectDraw and DirectSound, and only free-eggbert uses DirectPlay.
free-eggbert calls Blt at four sites and BltFast at six, Planet Blupi three and five; one Blt per game is CPixmap::Display(), the once-per-frame back-buffer-to-primary present.
That call-site pressure explains why DirectDraw is free-direct's most developed subsystem and why CNA's FREEDIRECT renderer is a 2D path.

Eighteen and seventeen BltFast occurrences include declarations, wrapper definitions and wrapper calls, while only six and five calls reach IDirectDrawSurface::BltFast; counting both levels double-counts, so call-site totals need a named population.

target.evidence: free-direct @934f72f docs/audit-24h-free-direct.md (correction of the 18/17 figures); docs/audit_ddraw.md

concepts.section: A pixel-format mismatch that never became a visible bug
concepts.text: Both games request an explicit display depth (8 or 16 bits in free-eggbert, 8 in Planet Blupi) but free-direct's SetDisplayMode only logs the depth, stores width and height, and the primary is 32-bit.

concepts.section: A pixel-format mismatch that never became a visible bug
concepts.text: The depth mismatch is harmless for the audited games because their off-screen surfaces follow a hard-coded 32-bit path; it is verified for these callers, not a general guarantee.

concepts.section: Color keying: implementation broader than observed use
concepts.text: Planet Blupi uses source colour keying at two call sites through one caching helper, each a single-value range matching white via a GetDC/SetPixel/Lock round trip rather than a palette index.

concepts.section: Color keying: implementation broader than observed use
concepts.text: free-direct implements low-to-high colour-key ranges (palette-index ranges on 8-bit, raw or RGB ranges on 32-bit surfaces), but the audited games exercise only the single-value case.

Planet Blupi's IsIconPixel is a per-click gameplay hit test through GetDC/ReleaseDC; GetDC wraps 32-bit surfaces directly and expands 8-bit surfaces through the palette, and a second GetDC returns DDERR_DCALREADYCREATED.

concepts.section: A performance audit adds exact costs to the same call sites
concepts.text: BltFast has no destination-size parameter, so every audited BltFast interface call in both games is a 1:1 copy.

concepts.section: A performance audit adds exact costs to the same call sites
concepts.text: Discovery benchmark (headless, SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy): one 640x480 32-bit BltFast took 0.715 ms vs 0.0244 ms memcpy (29.4x) in Release and 4.704 ms vs 0.0229 ms (205.8x) in the default unoptimised build.

concepts.section: A performance audit adds exact costs to the same call sites
concepts.text: Current free-direct: a top-level single-configuration build defaults to Release, and BlitFrom takes a per-row memcpy for unscaled, un-keyed, same-depth copies followed by an opaque-alpha fix-up; the follow-up benchmark measured 0.466 ms (14.8x).

target.evidence: free-direct @934f72f CMakeLists.txt (Release default condition); src/directdraw/DirectDrawSurface.cpp (BlitFrom fast path); archive/plan20260718.md (0.466 ms)

concepts.section: A performance audit adds exact costs to the same call sites
concepts.text: Because free-eggbert's CPixmap::Display() present can scale into a differently sized window, the fast path compares the two rectangles at run time instead of trusting the calling method.
tokens: comparing the two rectangles at run time

concepts.section: A performance audit adds exact costs to the same call sites
concepts.text: The audit found game-side dead code: free-eggbert's CPixmap::DrawMap(int, RECT, RECT) contains one Blt call but has no caller with that signature.
The only QueryInterface call in either game targets a DirectPlay object; free-direct's DirectDraw objects return DDERR_UNSUPPORTED, and DirectPlay scope comes only from free-eggbert.
Both games pass PCMWAVEFORMAT, whose wBitsPerSample sits at offset 16 versus 14 in WAVEFORMATEX on LP64, so free-direct reads the pointer as PCMWAVEFORMAT to avoid taking padding as the sample depth.

SetPan is only called on mono effects, and at the pin it clamps and stores the value while the gain helper computes left/right gains and discards them; only volume reaches SDL, and tests prove clamping and no-crash, not an audible pan.
free-eggbert's BASS-backed sound path sits behind a compile-time flag fixed to false, and each game carries a wave-loading source that only includes itself.
concepts.note: Kept as the audit's finding, attributed to free-direct's audit.

target.evidence: free-direct @934f72f docs/audit-24h-free-direct.md (dead paths); not re-read in the game sources

concepts.text: Every inspected sound-playback call passes zero looping flags, so neither game reaches DirectSound looping.
Neither game calls GetCurrentPosition; free-direct declares only SetCurrentPosition, whose SDL stream is not seekable, and the getter stays unimplemented until a caller needs it.
Neither game requests an 8-bit CreateSurface format, so BlitFrom's silent fall-through for mixed 8/32-bit copies is never exercised; it remains a limitation.

target.evidence: free-direct @934f72f src/directdraw/DirectDrawSurface.cpp (BlitFrom depth branches); NEXT.md Phase 14 audit

concepts.text: An untracked cna.md in the free-eggbert working tree (30,145 bytes, SHA-256 87b1e3de…, dated 2026-07-16) studies a native CNA port that removes free-direct/free-api; it calls the compatibility layer a bridge, not a destination.

concepts.section: Scope from a direct line count
concepts.text: The game is already C++ (about 31,773 lines, over 21,000 of them simulation and world logic); the study rewrites the platform-services layer and keeps decblupi, decmove, decblock, decdesign, decio and the tables recognisable as a comparison point.
The study keeps CPixmap's public shape across its 98 direct call sites and replaces only its implementation with Texture2D, RenderTarget2D and SpriteBatch.

SetTransparent2's colour-key range cannot be expressed in a CNJ texture: colorKey is exactly three 0-255 integers matched exactly and keyed to alpha 0, so a range needs a game-specific GetData/SetData pass.
Free Eggbert updates from a 50 ms timer (20 Hz) while CNA's Game defaults to 166,667 ticks, so without an explicit TargetElapsedTime the simulation runs about three times too fast.
The study maps the F5-F8 speed controls to 1, 2, 4 or 8 fixed 50 ms simulation steps per tick instead of shortening TargetElapsedTime, keeping every step the original size.
concepts.note: Corrected: the document lists 1/2/4/8 steps, not 2/4/8.

concepts.text: No CNA Song route accepts MIDI: SongImporter extensions, the XNB Song reader's probes and the media library index contain no .mid.

CNA's SDL_mixer build disables FluidSynth but leaves SDLMIXER_MIDI and SDLMIXER_MIDI_TIMIDITY at their default on, so a Timidity decoder is compiled below CNA; a Song mapping, instrument policy and retained test are missing.

Three MIDI options (pre-render against a SoundFont, a CNA-level route, a game-specific TinySoundFont service via free-api) with a staged recommendation: bridge first, pre-rendered for release, CNA route last.
The reconstruction's CNetwork::Receive reads into a 500-byte stack buffer, zeroes the destination and never copies the data; a game-side defect that makes it an unreliable multiplayer specification.
concepts.note: Game-side defect in the decompiled reconstruction, not a CNA or free-direct defect; recorded as not-an-issue for CNA.

concepts.text: Recommended renderer order: SDL_RENDERER first, FREEDIRECT as a differential bridge, then an independent GL run; the study's EASYGL name is now one of five GL profiles (typically OPENGLES3), and FREEDIRECT is a migration tool.
concepts.note: Corrected old EASYGL spelling to the current five GL identities.

target.evidence: cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake (EasyGL family's five GL identities; FREEDIRECT); free-eggbert cna.md (Backend choice)

concepts.text: Free Eggbert is GPL-3.0 and CNA is Ms-PL; distributing them linked needs a licensing review that neither the study nor the site performs.

The call-site method yields a narrower layer aligned with its target games and surfaces details an API-only reading misses; for a native port it finds seams, timing assumptions, evidence gaps and licensing questions first.

issues.text: No CNA Song route (SongImporter, XNB Song reader, media library) accepts Standard MIDI; a Timidity decoder is compiled beneath CNA but unmapped and untested.
CNJ Texture2D colorKey accepts one exact RGB triple, no range.
CNJ colour keying keeps the key RGB and sets alpha 0 (not transparent black), which adds the key colour under premultiplied AlphaBlend.
Sibling free-direct @934f72f: DirectSound SetPan computes gains and discards them although its README claims constant-power mono pan (not a CNA defect).
free-eggbert's CNetwork::Receive never copies received data: a defect of the decompiled game, not of CNA.
